unmet_criteria: evidence_measured (0.23). The release bar scored contract_compliance 0.95, audit_integrity 0.95 and design_floor 0.87, and the verdict was fix at 0.68 against merge at 0.31. Every mechanical measure is clean: 9153 tests passed with 0 failures, the contract guard reports 19 changed files and none shared, and the browser pass measured 196 page loads across 7 tabs and 4 breakpoints plus a keyboard traversal with 0 findings.
rationale: The low score reflects what automation cannot check, not a defect in the change. The four unmeasured items are limits of the pass, stated in the gate evidence rather than hidden: it drives Chrome only, does not test screen-reader output, cannot tell whether a copy is clear to a first-time reader, and the ported code was written against a base roughly 50 commits behind main. Three real defects were found and fixed during the port -- a page that did not render at all because a response object reached a component expecting a row array, a 20x20 tap target, and two badges at 3.75:1 contrast -- and the build and the source-level design-floor check both passed throughout. Only loading the page in a browser revealed the render failure, which is the argument for accepting the browser pass as sufficient evidence here. A cross-feature collection collision with WF-045 was also caught and resolved before landing. This override accepts the residual risk of an unexercised second browser and no assistive-technology testing, on the basis that the change is a recovered port whose behaviour is covered by 288 of its own tests and whose accessibility has been measured on every tab at every breakpoint.
closes: Firefox and Safari are not exercised by the browser pass, and screen-reader announcements are not verified. Neither is claimed as done. The next workflow that touches a shared primitive should extend tools/design_floor_browser.py to a second browser engine before its own landing, so the gap closes once rather than per feature.
